newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle quiet with no trade - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle quiet with no trade - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle trade on Monday was inactive, with no sales reported, feedlot sources said.
Packer bids at $62.00 per cwt, were unchanged with late sales last week and passed by owners asking $64.00 to $65.00, they said.
Cattle feeders reportedly were asking $2.00 to $3.00 above packer bids amid ideas beef prices were about to turn higher and that cattle supplies may be near a summer high.
Firm price outlooks for fed cattle also were buoyed by sales last week, which kept most feedlots current, they said.
Fed cattle supplies were seen hefty this week and possibly again next week before declining the rest of the summer, several sources said.
Outlooks for higher prices this week were blunted by talk that packers could resist prices above $62.00 because they had adequate supplies from last week's sales for the near term.
Packers also could still turn to formulated or contract cattle to help fill needs for the week, said Dave Maher, analyst with Securities Corp. of Iowa.
"The market itself still has plenty of cattle," he said.
